6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivCarveLocus
7	
8	/-!
9	# `DivScheme g = Z(♦)`: the carve locus as a closed subscheme of the Grassmannian pair (DDR-1)
10	
11	The glued carve locus of the DAT-D design (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 1): the
12	chart-wise loci `Z(♦) ⊆ Spec (R^I ⊗ R^J)` (`Picard/DivCarveLocus.lean`) assemble into a
13	closed subscheme of `grPair` through the mathlib ideal-sheaf machinery — `carveIdealSheaf`
14	is the kernel ideal sheaf of the disjoint family of chart loci (the largest ideal sheaf
15	vanishing on all of them, `⨅ over the pair atlas`), and `DivScheme` is its subscheme.
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveIdealSheaf`: the ideal sheaf `I_♦` on `grPair`.
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme`, `carveSchemeι`, `carveSchemeOver`: the generic glued
19	  locus, its closed immersion (mathlib's `IdealSheafData.subschemeι` instance), and its
20	  `Over (Spec k)` form.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme_exists_factor_of_le_ker` and
22	  `carveIdealSheaf_le_ker_of_factors`: the factoring criterion at chart tests — a test
23	  map through a pair chart killing the chart carve ideal factors (uniquely, by `Mono`)
24	  through `carveSchemeι`.
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme_hom_ext` (`divScheme_hom_ext`, DDR-7's tail): morphisms
26	  into the locus are determined by their composites with the closed immersion.
27	* **Campaign spellings**: `DivScheme`, `divSchemeι`, `divSchemeOver` at the DAT-D
28	  windows.
29	
30	The chart-value identification (`carveIdealSheaf.ideal (pair chart) = I_♦`-chart, the
31	`KeyChart` of the DD-R roadmap) rests on the landed gluing compatibility
32	(`carveIdeal_le_ker_of_specMap_pairChartMap_eq`); its remaining half is the app-level
33	localization bookkeeping and is left to the successor lane (see the inbox memory).
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe u
39	
40	open TensorProduct CategoryTheory
41	
42	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
43	
44	open Grassmannian
45	
46	section Generic
47	
48	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
49	variable {ι : Type u} (μ : ι → ((Fin r₁ → k) →ₗ[k] (Fin r₂ → k)))
50	
51	/-- **The carve ideal sheaf `I_♦`** on the Grassmannian pair: the largest ideal sheaf
52	vanishing on every chart-wise carve locus — the infimum of the kernels of the chart
53	loci mapped into `grPair`. -/
54	noncomputable def carveIdealSheaf : (grPair k g r₁ g r₂).IdealSheafData :=
55	  ⨅ c : (glueData k g r₁).J × (glueData k g r₂).J,
56	    (carveLocusToGrPair k g r₁ r₂ μ c.1 c.2).ker
57	
58	/-- **The glued carve locus `Z(♦)`** as a scheme: the subscheme of the carve ideal
59	sheaf on the Grassmannian pair. -/
60	noncomputable def carveScheme : Scheme :=
61	  (carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ).subscheme
62	
63	/-- **The closed immersion `Z(♦) ⟶ grPair`**. -/
64	noncomputable def carveSchemeι : carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ μ ⟶ grPair k g r₁ g r₂ :=
65	  (carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ).subschemeι
66	
67	instance isClosedImmersion_carveSchemeι :
68	    IsClosedImmersion (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ) :=
69	  inferInstanceAs (IsClosedImmersion (carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ).subschemeι)
70	
71	/-- The kernel of the closed immersion is the carve ideal sheaf. -/
72	theorem ker_carveSchemeι :
73	    (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ).ker = carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ :=
74	  Scheme.IdealSheafData.ker_subschemeι _
75	
76	/-- **`Z(♦)` as a test object of `Over (Spec k)`**. -/
77	noncomputable def carveSchemeOver : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
78	  Over.mk (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ ≫ grPairStructMap k g r₁ g r₂)
79	
80	/-- Each chart-wise carve locus maps to the glued locus over `grPair`. -/
81	theorem carveIdealSheaf_le_ker_carveLocusToGrPair
82	    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
83	    carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ ≤ (carveLocusToGrPair k g r₁ r₂ μ i j).ker :=
84	  iInf_le _ (i, j)
85	
86	/-- **The factoring criterion, existence half** (the chart-test universal property): a
87	test morphism through a pair chart whose chart map kills the chart carve ideal factors
88	through the closed immersion `carveSchemeι`. -/
89	theorem carveScheme_exists_factor_of_le_ker
90	    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
91	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S]
92	    (w : PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j →+* S)
93	    (hker : carveIdeal k g r₁ r₂ μ i j ≤ RingHom.ker w) :
94	    ∃ v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶ carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ μ,
95	      v ≫ carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ
96	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom w) ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j := by
97	  obtain ⟨φ, hφ, -⟩ := (ideal_le_ker_iff_factors _ w).mp hker
98	  have hfac : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom w) ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j
99	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ) ≫ carveLocusToGrPair k g r₁ r₂ μ i j := by
100	    rw [carveLocusToGrPair, carveLocusι]
101	    refine Eq.trans ?_ (Category.assoc _ _ _)
102	    refine congrArg (· ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j) ?_
103	    rw [← Spec.map_comp]
104	    exact (congrArg (fun ρ => Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ρ)) hφ).symm
105	  refine ⟨IsClosedImmersion.lift (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ)
106	    (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom w) ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j) ?_,
107	    IsClosedImmersion.lift_fac _ _ _⟩
108	  rw [ker_carveSchemeι, hfac]
109	  exact le_trans (carveIdealSheaf_le_ker_carveLocusToGrPair k g r₁ r₂ μ i j)
110	    (Scheme.Hom.le_ker_comp _ _)
111	
112	/-- **The factoring criterion, kernel half**: a test morphism factoring through the
113	closed immersion has the carve ideal sheaf in its kernel. -/
114	theorem carveIdealSheaf_le_ker_of_factors {T : Scheme.{u}} (u : T ⟶ grPair k g r₁ g r₂)
115	    (v : T ⟶ carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ μ) (hv : v ≫ carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ = u) :
116	    carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ ≤ u.ker := by
117	  rw [← hv, ← ker_carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ]
118	  exact Scheme.Hom.le_ker_comp _ _
119	
120	/-- **Hom-ext into `Z(♦)`** (the `divScheme_hom_ext` tail of DDR-7): morphisms into the
121	glued carve locus are determined by their composites with the closed immersion — closed
122	immersions are monomorphisms. -/
123	theorem carveScheme_hom_ext {T : Scheme.{u}} (u v : T ⟶ carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ μ)
124	    (h : u ≫ carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ = v ≫ carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ) : u = v :=
125	  (cancel_mono (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ)).mp h
126	
127	end Generic
128	
129	/-! ## The campaign spellings (the DAT-D windows) -/
130	
131	section Curve
132	
133	open Scheme
134	
135	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
136	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
137	variable (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
138	variable (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(divisorSections k B ⊤))
139	variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))
140	
141	/-- **`DivScheme g = Z(♦)`** (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 1): the glued carve locus
142	of the DAT-D two-window multiplication carve, a closed subscheme of the Grassmannian
143	pair `Gr(g, H_M) ×_k Gr(g, H_{M+s})` through `divSchemeι`. -/
144	noncomputable def DivScheme : Scheme :=
145	  carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)
146	
147	/-- **The closed immersion `divSchemeι : DivScheme g ⟶ grPair`**. -/
148	noncomputable def divSchemeι : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ grPair k g r₁ g r₂ :=
149	  carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)
150	
151	instance isClosedImmersion_divSchemeι :
152	    IsClosedImmersion (divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) :=
153	  isClosedImmersion_carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)
154	
155	/-- **`DivScheme g` as a test object of `Over (Spec k)`**. -/
156	noncomputable def divSchemeOver : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
157	  carveSchemeOver k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)
158	
159	/-- The DDR-1 factoring criterion at the campaign windows: a chart test killing `I_♦`
160	factors through `divSchemeι`. -/
161	theorem divScheme_exists_factor_of_le_ker
162	    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
163	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] (w : PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j →+* S)
164	    (hker : divCarveIdeal k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j ≤ RingHom.ker w) :
165	    ∃ v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶ DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
166	      v ≫ divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂
167	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom w) ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j :=
168	  carveScheme_exists_factor_of_le_ker k g r₁ r₂ _ i j w hker
169	
170	/-- **`divScheme_hom_ext`** (DDR-7): morphisms into `DivScheme g` are determined by
171	their composites with `divSchemeι`. -/
172	theorem divScheme_hom_ext {T : Scheme.{u}} (u v : T ⟶ DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)
173	    (h : u ≫ divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ = v ≫ divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) :
174	    u = v :=
175	  carveScheme_hom_ext k g r₁ r₂ _ u v h
176	
177	end Curve
178	
179	end AlgebraicGeometry
180

I want to know whether Sym^g C could be obtained as a REPRESENTING SCHEME of an already-representable functor in this tree, instead of via Milne's affine-and-glue quotient.

pullback–tensor comparison `Scheme.Modules.pullbackTensorMap` built in
`Picard/TensorObjSubstrate.lean` (the sheafified mate of the lax monoidal
structure of the pushforward) — together with the unit case `f^*𝒪_Z ≅ 𝒪_Y`,
which is `Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso` (the comparison functor on opens is
always `Final`).  The tensor `Scheme.Modules.tensorObj` is definitionally
equal to the section-graded `Scheme.Modules.sheafTensorObj` (both sheafify
the presheaf-level tensor of the underlying presheaves), so `asIso` of the
canonical comparison re-types at `sheafTensorObj` directly.  Invertibility of
that comparison, `Scheme.Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso` just below, is the
one statement of this section that remains unproved (blueprint
`lem:pullback_tensor_map_isiso`). -/

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- **The canonical pullback–tensor comparison is an isomorphism**
([Stacks 01CD] = Modules, Lemma `tensor-product-pullback`, which is
unconditional: the canonical comparison map is invertible for arbitrary
sheaves of modules on ringed spaces; stalkwise it is the base-change
isomorphism of tensor products, via [Stacks 01CB] + [Stacks 0098]): for a
morphism of schemes `f : Y ⟶ Z` and `A B : Z.Modules`, the sheaf-level
comparison `Scheme.Modules.pullbackTensorMap f A B :
f^*(A ⊗ B) ⟶ f^*A ⊗ f^*B` of `Picard/TensorObjSubstrate.lean` is an
isomorphism.

This statement is not proved here; it is one of the two obligations this file
leaves open.  The obstruction is that the Lean pullback functor is an
*abstract* left adjoint with no sectionwise value, so invertibility cannot be
checked on sections directly.  Three reductions of the statement are
available: (i) a chart-chase generalizing
`Modules.pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial` from trivializing charts to
affine charts, using `Modules.pullback_app_isoTensor` on the pullback side
and a `Γ(affine, tensorObj)` section formula for quasi-coherent factors, then
globalized by `isIso_of_isIso_restrict` through the restriction coherence
`Modules.pullbackTensorMap_restrict`; (ii) the concrete inverse-image model
`extendScalars ⋙ pullback₀` as a left Kan extension
(`sec:tensorobj_pullback_monoidality`); (iii) stalkwise, which needs stalk
machinery for `SheafOfModules` that Mathlib does not currently have (the
presheaf-level comparison map is in `TensorObjSubstrate/StalkTensor.lean`).
Blueprint: `lem:pullback_tensor_map_isiso`. -/
theorem Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ Z) (A B : Z.Modules) :
    IsIso (Modules.pullbackTensorMap f A B) := by
  sorry

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- **Pullback commutes with the binary sheaf tensor product**: the
`sheafTensorObj`-typed `Iso` packaging of `Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso`.
The tensor `Modules.tensorObj` and the section-graded
-----
`F_t ⊗ L_t^{⊗m}` along `Scheme.fiberBaseChange π ψ t'` equals the
`κ(t)`-dimension of the global sections of the twisted module itself — the
right-hand side being the graded Hilbert function of `F` at `t`.  Proper
support of `F` over `T` makes the (schematic) support of the twisted module
proper, in particular quasi-compact and separated, over the residue field, so
that [Stacks 02KH] applies to it; quasi-coherence of `L` (hence of the twist)
is likewise required.  In the infinite-dimensional case both sides carry the
junk value `0` of `Module.finrank`, matching the equality of infinite
dimensions.  Blueprint: `lem:gamma_fiber_baseChange_field`.

The scheme-level content is carried by
`Scheme.gammaFiber_finrank_baseChange_field_of_quasicoherent` above (transfer
of properness to the fibre, monotonicity of the support under twisting, and
the flat base-change statement for `Γ`,
`finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport` of
`Picard/SchematicSupport.lean`).  What is left unproved here, and is the
reason this declaration still uses `sorry`, is quasi-coherence of the
sheafified tensor `moduleTensorPow F_t L_t^{⊗m}` of quasi-coherent modules —
the affine tensor-section formula of `Picard/TensorSectionFormula.lean`
([Stacks 01CB]), the same input `lem:pullback_tensor_map_isiso` needs. -/
theorem gammaFiber_finrank_baseChange_field (π : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules)
    [L.IsQuasicoherent] {T T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T)
    (F : (Limits.pullback π T.hom).Modules) (hfp : F.IsFinitePresentation)
    (hps : Modules.HasProperSupport (pullback.snd π T.hom) F)
    (t' : (T'.left : Scheme.{u})) (m : ℕ) :
    (letI := (pullback.snd π T'.hom).fiberSectionsModule t'
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (fiberBaseChange π ψ t')).obj
          (Scheme.Modules.moduleTensorPow
            ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule (ψ.left.base t') F)
            ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule (ψ.left.base t')
              ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L)) m))
     Module.finrank (T'.left.residueField t')
        Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (fiberBaseChange π ψ t')).obj
          (Scheme.Modules.moduleTensorPow
            ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule (ψ.left.base t') F)
            ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule (ψ.left.base t')
              ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L)) m), ⊤))
      = hilbertFunction (pullback.snd π T.hom)
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) F
          (ψ.left.base t') m := by
  refine gammaFiber_finrank_baseChange_field_of_quasicoherent π L ψ F hfp hps t' m ?_
  -- Remaining obligation (`lem:gamma_fiber_baseChange_field`): quasi-coherence
  -- of the sheafified tensor of quasi-coherent modules (Stacks 01CB), i.e. the

cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
echo "=== sorry count per DivRep/DivScheme/Div* file ==="
for f in AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivRep*.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivScheme*.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamily*.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/PicRepDatum.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/PicRepColimit*.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean; do
  n=$(grep -c '\bsorry\b' "$f" 2>/dev/null)
  bare=$(grep -c '^\s*sorry\s*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$f : sorry-mentions=$n bare-sorry=$bare"
done

8	
9	/-!
10	# Degree slices of the relative-divisor functor + the degree-refined Abel map
11	
12	Campaign milestones **D1'** (degree-`d` divisor functor `DivFunctorDeg`, clopen
13	degree decomposition, base-change stability of the fibre degree) and **A2**
14	(degree-refined Abel map `abelDeg`) of the `instHasPicScheme` campaign
15	(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), on top of the landed divisor
16	functor `Scheme.DivFunctor` (Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §3 Def. `df:div`;
17	`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`).
18	
19	## The fibre degree
20	
21	For a family of relative effective divisors `x : DivFamily π T` (the quotient
22	encoding: `q : O_{X_T} ↠ F = O_D` with invertible kernel ideal `I_D = ker q`),
23	the **fibre degree** at `t : T` is
24	
25	  `x.fiberDeg t := dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t}) = dim_{κ(t)} Γ((X_T)_t, F_t)`,
26	
27	Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`'s degree of the fibre divisor `D_t ⊆ X_t` — the
28	`H⁰`-only, cohomology-free rank.
29	
30	**AUDIT (encoding choice, D1').** The campaign phrase "rank-`d` of the
31	finite-flat pushforward of `O_D`" is realized by its *pointwise shadow*: the
32	in-tree substrate has no `q_* O_D`-as-locally-free-object (that is exactly the
33	B3 rigid-pushforward engine, unbuilt), and for a finite flat family the rank of
34	the pushforward at `t` *equals* `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t})` (pushforward along
35	an affine morphism is exact and commutes with base change).  The fibre-section
36	form is honest at full generality (any `π`, any `T`; `Module.finrank` junk
37	value `0` if the fibre sections are infinite-dimensional, which does not occur
38	for divisor fibres in the relative-curve regime) and is what Kleiman's
39	`deg D_t` means.  When B3 lands, `q_* O_D` is locally free of rank
40	`fiberDeg` and the two vocabularies fuse.
41	
42	**AUDIT (base change, D1').** `fiberDeg` is stable under arbitrary base change
43	`ψ : T' ⟶ T` (`fiberDeg_pullbackAlong`): the fibre of `X_{T'}/T'` at `t'` is
44	the base change of the fibre of `X_T/T` at `t = ψ(t')` along the residue
45	extension `κ(t) → κ(t')`, and `H⁰` of a finitely presented module with proper
46	support commutes with base field extension (Stacks 02KH at `i = 0`).  This is
47	proved **axiom-clean** from the twist-free Γ-fibre core
48	`Scheme.finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport`
49	(`Picard/SchematicSupport.lean`) — NOT from the twisted engine
50	`Scheme.hilbertFunction_quotBaseMap` (`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean`), which
51	still rests on the sorried tensor–pullback leaf
52	`Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso`.  At `m = 0` no twist is needed, so the
53	degree lane stays sorry-free (recon correction to the campaign plan's
54	"the 02KE/02KH engine is landed" — only its untwisted core is).
55	
56	## The clopen degree decomposition — honest form
57	
58	**AUDIT (coproduct pin, D1').** The naive presheaf-level statement
59	"`DivFunctor = ⨿_d DivFunctorDeg d`" is FALSE: on a disconnected `T` a family
60	with non-constant fibre degree lies in no degree piece, and at `T = ∅` every
61	piece contains the (unique) empty family, so the pieces are not disjoint.  The
62	honest pins delivered here are:
63	
64	* every `T`-point decomposes `T` into clopen constant-degree pieces
65	  (`DivFamily.degLocus`, `DivFamily.hasFiberDeg_pullbackAlong_degLocusHom`,
66	  `DivFamily.iSup_degLocus`, `DivFamily.degLocus_disjoint`) — this is the form
67	  the coproduct assembly `G4` (`hom_sigma_decompose`) consumes;
68	* on a nonempty preconnected `T` the canonical comparison
69	  `Σ_d (DivFunctorDeg π d)(T) → DivFunctor π (T)` is a bijection
70	  (`divFunctorDeg_sigma_bijective`);
71	* degree pieces of a common class agree (`DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.unique`,
72	  nonempty `T`).
73	
74	The only non-formal input is **Zariski-local constancy of the fibre degree**.
75	This is TRUE in the campaign regime (relative curve: `D → T` is
76	proper + quasi-finite, hence finite, and a finitely presented `T`-flat module
77	with finite support has finite locally free pushforward — Mumford, *Abelian
78	Varieties* II §5; Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`) but is NOT derivable from the
79	current in-tree substrate (it needs the finite/rank half of the B3 pushforward
80	engine plus `D_t` finite from relative dimension 1).  Following the house gate
81	pattern (`HasPicScheme`), it is pinned as the instance-free Prop-class
82	`HasLocallyConstantDivDeg C` at the AJC curve regime, and every decomposition
83	statement is ALSO provided in hypothesis-parametrized form (an explicit
84	`IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg` argument), so the eventual discharge is a
85	one-line instance.  We deliberately do NOT state the gate for general `π`:
86	for relative dimension `≥ 2` the fibre rank of `O_{D_t}` can jump (only `χ` is
87	locally constant), which is why Kleiman filters `Div` by Hilbert polynomials in
88	general and by the degree only over curves.
89	
90	## The degree ledger and the Abel-map sign (A2)
91	
92	**Sign convention (audit item 7-half).** The Abel map is
93	`abelMapWitness C = abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, i.e.
94	
95	  `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[ker q]`  —
96	
97	a divisor family maps to the *negative* of the class of its ideal sheaf
98	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:461`).  The degree-refined Abel map
99	`abelDeg C d : divFunctorDeg C d ⟶ picSharp C` is the restriction of
100	`abelMapWitness` along the degree-`d` inclusion; its defining property is
101	`abelDeg_app_mk`.  It deliberately lands in `picSharp C` — carving out
102	`picSharpDeg C d` is milestone B4, not this file.
103	
104	**AUDIT (degree-coherence vocabulary, A2).** "The ideal sheaf `ker q` of a
105	rank-`d` family has fibre degree `−d`" is stated in the **rank (colength)
106	vocabulary** — the strongest honestly-provable form today: the χ-ledger
107	(`deg = χ(I) − χ(O)`, campaign P3) is unbuilt, and the adelic
108	`RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor` degree cannot yet be attached to the sheaf-theoretic
109	line bundle `ker q` on a family fibre (that needs the `M ≅ O(div s)`
110	regular-section bricks, also P3).  What IS proved, per fibre `t`:
111	
112	* the ideal restricts to the fibre: the kernel–pullback comparison
113	  `(I_D)_t ≅ ker(q_t)` is an isomorphism (`DivFamily.fiberKernelIso`) and the
114	  fibre ideal inclusion `(I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t}` stays monic
115	  (`DivFamily.mono_fiber_kernel_ι`) with `(I_D)_t` invertible
116	  (`DivFamily.isLocallyTrivial_fiber_kernel`) — `D_t ⊆ X_t` is an honest
117	  effective Cartier divisor (Kleiman §3, note after Def. `df:div`);
118	* its colength is the degree: `O_{X_t}/(I_D)_t ≅ (O_D)_t`
119	  (`DivFamily.fiberCokernelIso`), so
120	  `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(coker((I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t})) = fiberDeg x t = d`
121	  (`DivFamily.fiberDeg_eq_finrank_fiber_cokernel`,
122	  `DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.finrank_fiber_cokernel`).
123	
124	In χ-ledger terms this is exactly `deg_t(ker q) = χ(I_t) − χ(O_{X_t}) = −d`;
125	the translation becomes a theorem once P3 lands.

161	    (letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G

163	      = (letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G'

171	    { toFun := γe
172	      map_add' := γe.map_add
173	      map_smul' := fun c x => γe.map_smul ((π₀.fiberResidueMap s).hom c) x
174	      invFun := γe.symm

384	  ∀ t : (T.left : Scheme.{u}), x.fiberDeg t = d
385	
386	/-- Constant fibre degree is invariant under the divisor equivalence
387	(`DivFamily.Rel`): well-definedness input for the degree slice of the
388	quotient functor. -/
389	theorem Rel.hasFiberDeg_iff {T : Over S} {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y)
390	    (d : ℕ) : x.HasFiberDeg d ↔ y.HasFiberDeg d :=
391	  forall_congr' fun t => by rw [h.fiberDeg_eq t]
392	
393	/-- Constant fibre degree is stable under arbitrary base change — the degree
394	slice `DivFunctorDeg` is a subfunctor, not just a sub-presheaf-of-sets.
395	Immediate from `fiberDeg_pullbackAlong`. -/
396	theorem HasFiberDeg.pullbackAlong {T T' : Over S} {x : DivFamily π T} {d : ℕ}
397	    (hx : x.HasFiberDeg d) (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
398	    (x.pullbackAlong ψ).HasFiberDeg d :=
399	  fun t' => (fiberDeg_pullbackAlong ψ x t').trans (hx (ψ.left.base t'))
400	
401	/-- Constant fibre degree, descended to the divisor classes
402	`Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)` — the carrier predicate of
403	`DivFunctorDeg π d`.  Well defined by `Rel.hasFiberDeg_iff`. -/
404	def ClassHasFiberDeg {T : Over S} (d : ℕ)
405	    (z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)) : Prop :=
406	  Quotient.liftOn z (fun x => x.HasFiberDeg d)
407	    fun _ _ h => propext (h.hasFiberDeg_iff d)
408	
409	@[simp]
410	theorem classHasFiberDeg_mk {T : Over S} (d : ℕ) (x : DivFamily π T) :
411	    ClassHasFiberDeg d (Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid π T) x) ↔ x.HasFiberDeg d :=
412	  Iff.rfl
413	
414	/-- Base-change stability of the class-level degree predicate — the
415	functoriality input of `DivFunctorDeg`. -/
416	theorem ClassHasFiberDeg.map {T T' : Over S} {d : ℕ}
417	    {z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)} (hz : ClassHasFiberDeg d z)
418	    (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
419	    ClassHasFiberDeg d (Quotient.map (DivFamily.pullbackAlong ψ)
420	      (fun _ _ h => DivFamily.pullbackAlong_rel ψ h) z) := by
421	  induction z using Quotient.ind with
422	  | _ x =>
423	    intro t'
424	    exact (fiberDeg_pullbackAlong ψ x t').trans (hz (ψ.left.base t'))
425	
426	/-- **Over a nonempty base the degree of a class is unique** — the degree
427	pieces of `DivFunctor` are pairwise disjoint on nonempty `T` (and only there:
428	at `T = ∅` every class has every degree, see the module docstring audit). -/
429	theorem ClassHasFiberDeg.unique {T : Over S}
430	    (hne : Nonempty (T.left : Scheme.{u})) {d d' : ℕ}
431	    {z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)}
432	    (h : ClassHasFiberDeg d z) (h' : ClassHasFiberDeg d' z) : d = d' := by
433	  induction z using Quotient.ind with
434	  | _ x =>
435	    obtain ⟨t⟩ := hne
436	    exact (h t).symm.trans (h' t)
437	
438	/-- **Degree side of the A2 sign audit** (rank vocabulary — see the module
439	docstring audit): a representative of a degree-`d` divisor class has, at
440	every point `t` of `T`, fibre ideal of colength `d`:
441	
442	  `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(X_t, coker((I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t})) = d`.
443	
444	Combined with the sign convention `[D] ↦ -[ker q]` of the Abel map
445	(`PicScheme.abelDeg_app_mk`) this is the honest content of "the ideal sheaf
446	`ker q` of a rank-`d` family has fibre degree `−d`" available before the P3
447	χ-ledger lands. -/
448	theorem ClassHasFiberDeg.finrank_fiber_cokernel {T : Over S} {d : ℕ}
449	    (x : DivFamily π T)
450	    (hx : ClassHasFiberDeg d (Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid π T) x))
451	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
452	    (letI := (pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberSectionsModule t
453	        (Limits.cokernel
454	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map
455	            (Limits.kernel.ι x.q)))
456	     Module.finrank (T.left.residueField t)
457	      Γ(Limits.cokernel
458	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map
459	            (Limits.kernel.ι x.q)), ⊤))
460	      = d :=
461	  (x.fiberDeg_eq_finrank_fiber_cokernel t).symm.trans (hx t)
462	
463	end DivFamily
464	
465	/-! ## §4. The degree-`d` divisor functor -/
466	
467	/-- The **degree-`d` relative-divisor functor** `Div^d_{X/S} ⊆ Div_{X/S}`
468	(Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`): the subfunctor of `Scheme.DivFunctor π` of divisor
469	classes whose every fibre divisor has degree `d`
470	(`DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg`, the rank-`d`-pushforward condition in its
471	pointwise fibre-section form — see the module docstring audit).  The pullback
472	action is that of `DivFunctor`, restricted along the base-change stability
473	`DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.map`; the functor laws are inherited pointwise
474	from `DivFunctor`.
475	
476	Kept at full generality (`π : X ⟶ S` arbitrary, matching `DivFunctor`); in
477	the FGA regime (`π` proper, `[IsProper C.hom]`) the `properSupport` field of
478	`DivFamily` is automatic, so the `T`-points are honestly Kleiman's degree-`d`
479	relative effective divisors. -/
480	noncomputable def DivFunctorDeg (π : X ⟶ S) (d : ℕ) :
481	    (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1) where
482	  obj T := { z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T.unop) //
483	    DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg d z }
484	  map {T T'} g := TypeCat.ofHom fun z =>
485	    ⟨Quotient.map (DivFamily.pullbackAlong g.unop)
486	        (fun _ _ h => DivFamily.pullbackAlong_rel g.unop h) z.1,
487	      z.2.map g.unop⟩
488	  map_id T := by
489	    ext z
490	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun f => ((TypeCat.Hom.hom f : TypeCat.Fun _ _) : _ → _))
491	      ((DivFunctor π).map_id T)) z.1
492	  map_comp {T T' T''} g h := by
493	    ext z
494	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun f => ((TypeCat.Hom.hom f : TypeCat.Fun _ _) : _ → _))
495	      ((DivFunctor π).map_comp g h)) z.1
496	
497	/-- The canonical inclusion `Div^d_{X/S} ⟶ Div_{X/S}` — the subfunctor
498	inclusion of the degree-`d` slice, forgetting the constant-degree witness.
499	Componentwise injective (`divFunctorDegι_app_injective`). -/
500	noncomputable def divFunctorDegι (π : X ⟶ S) (d : ℕ) :
501	    DivFunctorDeg π d ⟶ DivFunctor π where
502	  app _ := TypeCat.ofHom Subtype.val
503	  naturality _ _ _ := rfl
504	
505	/-- The degree-`d` inclusion is componentwise injective: `DivFunctorDeg π d`
506	is a subfunctor of `DivFunctor π`. -/
507	theorem divFunctorDegι_app_injective (π : X ⟶ S) (d : ℕ)
508	    (T : (Over S)ᵒᵖ) :
509	    Function.Injective ((divFunctorDegι π d).app T : _ → _) :=
510	  fun _ _ h => Subtype.ext h
511	
512	/-! ## §5. The clopen degree decomposition -/
513	
514	namespace DivFamily
515	
516	variable {π : X ⟶ S}
517	
518	/-- The **degree-`d` locus** of a divisor family with locally constant fibre
519	degree: the clopen open subset `{t : T | deg D_t = d}` of the base.  The
520	local-constancy hypothesis is explicit (its discharge in the relative-curve
521	regime is the `HasLocallyConstantDivDeg` gate — see the module docstring). -/
522	def degLocus {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
523	    (hlc : IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) (d : ℕ) : (T.left : Scheme.{u}).Opens :=
524	  ⟨{t | x.fiberDeg t = d}, hlc.isOpen_fiber d⟩
525	
526	/-- The degree-`d` locus is clopen. -/
527	theorem isClopen_degLocus {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
528	    (hlc : IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) (d : ℕ) :
529	    IsClopen ((x.degLocus hlc d : TopologicalSpace.Opens (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
530	      Set (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :=
531	  hlc.isClopen_fiber d
532	
533	/-- The degree loci cover the base: every point lies in the locus of its own
534	fibre degree. -/
535	theorem iSup_degLocus {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
536	    (hlc : IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) :
537	    ⨆ d : ℕ, x.degLocus hlc d = ⊤ := by
538	  rw [eq_top_iff]
539	  intro t _
540	  exact TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨x.fiberDeg t, rfl⟩
541	
542	/-- The degree loci are pairwise disjoint: the fibre degree is a single
543	natural number at every point. -/
544	theorem degLocus_disjoint {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
545	    (hlc : IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) {d d' : ℕ} (h : d ≠ d') :
546	    Disjoint (x.degLocus hlc d) (x.degLocus hlc d') := by
547	  refine disjoint_iff.mpr (TopologicalSpace.Opens.ext ?_)
548	  ext t
549	  simp only [TopologicalSpace.Opens.coe_inf, Set.mem_inter_iff,
550	    TopologicalSpace.Opens.coe_bot, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false, not_and]
551	  intro h1 h2
552	  exact h ((show x.fiberDeg t = d from h1).symm.trans
553	    (show x.fiberDeg t = d' from h2))
554	
555	/-- The clopen immersion of the degree-`d` locus, as a morphism of `Over S`:
556	the piece of the clopen decomposition along which the family restricts to a
557	constant-degree family (`hasFiberDeg_pullbackAlong_degLocusHom`). -/
558	noncomputable def degLocusHom {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
559	    (hlc : IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) (d : ℕ) :
560	    Over.mk ((x.degLocus hlc d).ι ≫ T.hom) ⟶ T :=
561	  Over.homMk (x.degLocus hlc d).ι rfl
562	
563	/-- **Every `T`-point of `Div` decomposes `T` into clopen constant-degree
564	pieces** (the honest form of `Div = ∐_d Div^d`, per-family half): the
565	restriction of the family to its degree-`d` locus has constant fibre degree
566	`d`.  Together with `iSup_degLocus`/`degLocus_disjoint`/`isClopen_degLocus`
567	this is the clopen decomposition the coproduct assembly (campaign G4)
568	consumes. -/
569	theorem hasFiberDeg_pullbackAlong_degLocusHom {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
570	    (hlc : IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) (d : ℕ) :
571	    (x.pullbackAlong (x.degLocusHom hlc d)).HasFiberDeg d := by
572	  intro t'
573	  rw [fiberDeg_pullbackAlong]
574	  exact t'.2
575	
576	end DivFamily
577	
578	/-- **`Div = ∐_d Div^d` on connected bases** (the honest functor-level form of
579	the degree decomposition — see the module docstring audit for why the
580	unrestricted presheaf statement is false): over a nonempty preconnected `T`,
581	the canonical comparison `Σ_d Div^d(T) → Div(T)` is a bijection, granted the
582	local constancy of fibre degrees (hypothesis-parametrized; in the AJC curve
583	regime it is the `HasLocallyConstantDivDeg` gate, see
584	`divFunctorDeg_sigma_bijective_of_gate`).  Injectivity is degree-uniqueness on
585	a nonempty base; surjectivity is "locally constant on preconnected = constant"
586	(`IsLocallyConstant.apply_eq_of_preconnectedSpace`). -/
587	theorem divFunctorDeg_sigma_bijective (π : X ⟶ S) {T : (Over S)ᵒᵖ}
588	    (hne : Nonempty (T.unop.left : Scheme.{u}))
589	    (hpc : PreconnectedSpace (T.unop.left : Scheme.{u}))
590	    (hlc : ∀ x : DivFamily π T.unop, IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) :
591	    Function.Bijective fun p : (Σ d : ℕ, (DivFunctorDeg π d).obj T) =>
592	      (p.2.1 : (DivFunctor π).obj T) := by
593	  constructor
594	  · rintro ⟨d, z, hz⟩ ⟨d', z', hz'⟩ h
595	    obtain rfl : z = z' := h
596	    obtain rfl : d = d' := DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.unique hne hz hz'
597	    rfl
598	  · intro z
599	    induction z using Quotient.ind with
600	    | _ x =>
601	      obtain ⟨t₀⟩ := hne
602	      haveI := hpc
603	      exact ⟨⟨x.fiberDeg t₀, ⟨Quotient.mk _ x,
604	        fun t => (hlc x).apply_eq_of_preconnectedSpace t t₀⟩⟩, rfl⟩
605	
606	/-! ## §6. The local-constancy gate (relative-curve regime) -/
607	
608	/-- **Gate: divisor families on the curve have locally constant fibre degree**
609	(instance-free Prop-class, house `HasPicScheme` pattern — the deep heart is
610	deferred, never sorried).
611	
612	Mathematical content (TRUE at this pinned generality; Mumford, *Abelian
613	Varieties* II §5; Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`): for a smooth proper relative
614	curve `C/k` and any `T`, a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` is finite
615	flat over `T` (proper + quasi-finite: each `D_t` is the zero scheme of a
616	regular section of an invertible ideal on the curve `C_t`, hence
617	`0`-dimensional), so `q_* O_D` is finite locally free and its fibre rank —
618	`DivFamily.fiberDeg` — is Zariski-locally constant.  Discharge route: the
619	finiteness/rank half of the campaign's B3 rigid-pushforward engine plus
620	relative-dimension-1 quasi-finiteness; both are outside the current in-tree
621	substrate, hence the gate.
622	
623	Deliberately NOT stated for general `π : X ⟶ S`: in relative dimension `≥ 2`
624	the fibre rank of `O_{D_t}` can jump (only `χ(O_{D_t})` is locally constant),
625	which is why Kleiman filters `Div` by Hilbert polynomials in general.  All
626	decomposition theorems are also available in hypothesis-parametrized form
627	(explicit `IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg` argument), so this class is a pure
628	convenience pin at the AJC regime. -/
629	class HasLocallyConstantDivDeg {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
630	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] : Prop where
631	  /-- Every divisor family on the relative curve has Zariski-locally constant
632	  fibre degree. -/
633	  isLocallyConstant : ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (x : DivFamily C.hom T),
634	    IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg
635	
636	/-- `Div_{C/k} = ∐_d Div^d_{C/k}` on nonempty connected bases, gated form:
637	the sigma comparison is bijective for the AJC curve, granted the
638	`HasLocallyConstantDivDeg` gate. -/
639	theorem divFunctorDeg_sigma_bijective_of_gate {k : Type u} [Field k]
640	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
641	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
642	    [HasLocallyConstantDivDeg C] {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
643	    (hne : Nonempty (T.unop.left : Scheme.{u}))
644	    (hpc : PreconnectedSpace (T.unop.left : Scheme.{u})) :
645	    Function.Bijective fun p : (Σ d : ℕ, (DivFunctorDeg C.hom d).obj T) =>
646	      (p.2.1 : (DivFunctor C.hom).obj T) :=
647	  divFunctorDeg_sigma_bijective C.hom hne hpc
648	    (fun x => HasLocallyConstantDivDeg.isLocallyConstant T.unop x)
649	
650	/-! ## §7. A2 — the degree-refined Abel map -/
651	
652	namespace PicScheme
653	
654	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
655	
656	/-- The degree-`d` relative-divisor functor of the AJC curve,
657	`Div^d_{C/k} := DivFunctorDeg C.hom d` — the A.2.c-side avatar of the general
658	degree slice, mirroring `divFunctor C = DivFunctor C.hom`
659	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`). -/
660	noncomputable def divFunctorDeg (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (d : ℕ) :
661	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1) :=
662	  DivFunctorDeg C.hom d
663	
664	/-- **The degree-refined Abel map** `A^d_{C/k} : Div^d_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`
665	(Kleiman §3 Def. `dfn:Abel`, restricted to the degree-`d` slice): the
666	composite of the degree-`d` inclusion with the substantive Abel map
667	`abelMapWitness C`, so on points
668	
669	  `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[ker q]`  (defining property `abelDeg_app_mk`).
670	
671	Sign convention (audit item 7-half): the divisor class maps to the **negative**
672	of the ideal-sheaf class; the fibre-degree ledger for the ideal side is
673	`DivFamily.fiberDeg_eq_finrank_fiber_cokernel` ("`ker q` has fibre degree
674	`−d`" in the rank vocabulary — module docstring audit).  The target is
675	deliberately the full `picSharp C`: carving out the degree-`d` Picard
676	subfunctor `picSharpDeg C d` is campaign milestone B4, and refactoring
677	`abelDeg` to corestrict onto it is part of that milestone, not this one. -/
678	noncomputable def abelDeg (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
679	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] (d : ℕ) :
680	    divFunctorDeg C d ⟶ picSharp C :=
681	  divFunctorDegι C.hom d ≫ abelMapWitness C
682	
683	/-- **Defining property of the degree-refined Abel map** (Kleiman §3
684	Def. `dfn:Abel`): on the class of a degree-`d` divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` it
685	returns `[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹]`, the additive inverse of the class of the ideal
686	sheaf `I_D = ker q` — the `[D] ↦ -[ker q]` sign convention, verbatim
687	compatible with `abelMap_app_mk` through the inclusion. -/
688	theorem abelDeg_app_mk (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
689	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] (d : ℕ)
690	    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (x : DivFamily C.hom T.unop)
691	    (hx : DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg d
692	      (Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid C.hom T.unop) x)) :
693	    (abelDeg C d).app T ⟨Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid C.hom T.unop) x, hx⟩ =
694	      - Quotient.mk (PicSharp.relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
695	        (⟨kernel x.q, x.kerLocallyTrivial⟩ :
696	          LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom) :=
697	  rfl
698	
699	/-- The degree-refined Abel map factors the Abel map witness through the
700	degree-`d` inclusion — definitional, recorded for the blueprint. -/
701	theorem abelDeg_eq (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
702	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] (d : ℕ) :
703	    abelDeg C d = divFunctorDegι C.hom d ≫ abelMapWitness C :=
704	  rfl
705	
706	end PicScheme
707	
708	end Scheme
709	
710	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.

4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarC1
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarTransport
9	
10	/-!
11	# The chart-confinement obstruction in witness form
12	
13	`DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean` establishes the verdict positively: a certified adaptation of a
14	connected divisor confines its support to one pinned chart
15	(`supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified`).  Its contrapositive is recorded there only for
16	the *leak-free* hypothesis and only in "not contained in either chart" form.
17	
18	This file states the obstruction in the form a would-be user of the interface meets it: with
19	two **witness points** of the support, one off `V₀` and one off `V₁`.  That is the shape in
20	which a concrete divisor — e.g. one whose fibre over a base point is `{0, ∞}` — refutes
21	certifiability, and it needs no leak hypothesis.
22	
23	Combined with the pullback transport (`DivSchemeCertZarTransport.lean`), which shows support
24	loci pull back along the base-shrinking maps, the obstruction is visibly Zariski-local on the
25	base: shrinking cannot separate the two witnesses.
26	
27	## Main declarations
28	
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses` — a
30	  connected divisor with a support point off each pinned chart admits no certified adaptation,
31	  in any degree.
32	-/
33	
34	set_option autoImplicit false
35	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
36	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161); pin in-file. -/
37	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
38	
39	universe u
40	
41	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
42	
43	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
44	
45	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
46	
47	namespace DivisorAdaptation
48	
49	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
50	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
51	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
52	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
53	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)
54	
55	/-- **The obstruction in witness form.** If the support is connected and contains a point
56	outside `V₀` and a point outside `V₁` — i.e. the divisor genuinely meets both `pi⁻¹(∞)` and
57	`pi⁻¹(0)` — then `A` carries no certificate, in any degree.
58	
59	No leak hypothesis: clause (c1) of `IsCertified` supplies it
60	(`supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength`).  So the interface does not merely make such
61	divisors hard to certify, it excludes them. -/
62	theorem not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses {n : ℕ}
63	    (hconn : _root_.IsPreconnected d.supportLocus)
64	    {x y : relCurve C R} (hx : x ∈ d.supportLocus) (hy : y ∈ d.supportLocus)
65	    (hx₀ : x ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))
66	    (hy₁ : y ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) :

11	
12	/-!
13	# The relative-divisor functor `Div_{X/S}` (real definition)
14	
15	This file constructs the relative-effective-divisor functor
16	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.DivFunctor π : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1)` of Kleiman,
17	"The Picard scheme", §3 (Def. `df:red` + Def. `df:div`; FGA Explained Ch. 9,
18	arXiv:math/0504020), the source of the Abel map of the A.2.c FGA assembly
19	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, whose `divFunctor` carrier this file
20	makes real).
21	
22	## Encoding decision (quotient encoding)
23	
24	Kleiman §3 Def. `df:red`/`df:div`: a *relative effective divisor* on `X_T/T`
25	is a closed subscheme `D ⊆ X_T` whose ideal `I` is **invertible** and which is
26	**`T`-flat**; `Div_{X/S}(T)` is the set of such `D`.  We encode a divisor by
27	its structure-sheaf quotient — the same encoding by which `Div ⊆ Hilb =
28	Quot_{O}` sits inside the Quot functor (Kleiman §3 Thm. `th:repDiv`): a
29	`DivFamily π T` is a `Scheme.QuotFamily`-shaped structure with `E` the unit
30	module `O_X` (so `q : O_{X_T} ⟶ F` up to the canonical isomorphism
31	`(pr₁)^* O_X ≅ O_{X_T}`; we state the source of `q` verbatim as the pullback
32	of the unit, exactly as `QuotFamily` does for a general `E`, so that the whole
33	pullback/functoriality skeleton of `QuotFunctorDef.lean` is reusable), and the
34	**divisor condition** is: the kernel ideal `I = ker q` is invertible, encoded
35	by the project-side line-bundle predicate
36	`Scheme.LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (kernel q)` (locally trivial of rank one,
37	Stacks 01HK — the same predicate that carves the line bundles out of
38	`Scheme.Modules` in `Picard/LineBundlePullback.lean`).  Between the two
39	candidate encodings of invertibility (a bundled mono `ι : I ⟶ O` with a
40	cokernel identification, versus the predicate on the categorical kernel) we
41	choose the **kernel predicate**: `X.Modules` is abelian, so `ker q` is
42	available functorially with no extra data fields, the equivalence relation on
43	families stays literally that of the Quot functor (`ker q = ker q'` — no
44	well-definedness burden for extra fields), and invertibility-of-an-object is
45	exactly what `IsLocallyTrivial` and its proved pullback-stability
46	(`IsLocallyTrivial.pullback`, Stacks 01HH) speak about.
47	
48	Two families are equivalent iff an isomorphism of the targets commutes with
49	the quotient maps — equivalently `ker q = ker q'` as subobjects of `O_{X_T}`,
50	i.e. the two quotients cut out the same closed subscheme `D`.  The value
51	`DivFunctor π |_T` is the quotient by this relation, so it is Kleiman's *set*
52	of relative effective divisors on `X_T/T`, not a groupoid of quotients.
53	
54	Faithfulness notes (Kleiman §3):
55	
56	* the fields `isFinitePresentation` and `properSupport` do not shrink the set
57	  of divisors in the intended regime: `F = O_D = coker(I ⟶ O)` with `I`
58	  invertible is automatically finitely presented, and for the FGA
59	  instantiation (`π` proper, e.g. the curve `C/k`) the schematic support `D`
60	  is a closed subscheme of the `T`-proper `X_T`, hence automatically proper
61	  over `T`.  They are included to keep the family shape identical to
62	  `QuotFamily` (Div sits inside Hilb) and to reuse its base-change lemmas
63	  verbatim;
64	* there is **no Hilbert-polynomial field**: Kleiman's `Div_{X/S}` (`df:div`)
65	  is not filtered by `Φ` — the degree decomposition `Div = ∐_m Div^m`
66	  (Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`) is a later, separate refinement;
67	* no hypotheses on `π` are needed for the *functor* (Kleiman `df:div` imposes
68	  none; projectivity/flatness enter only in the representability theorem
69	  `th:repDiv`, which is not stated in this file).
70	
71	## Base-change well-definedness
72	
73	The pullback action reuses the `QuotFamily` base-change lemmas for the shared
74	fields (finite presentation: `Modules.pullback_isFinitePresentation`, proved;
75	flatness: `CoherentSheafFlat.of_isPullback`, proved; proper support:
76	`Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback`, proved in
77	`Picard/QuotSupportBaseChange.lean`) and needs exactly one new fact for the
78	divisor condition, proved in this file as the theorem
79	`Scheme.Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial` (blueprint
80	`lem:relative_divisor_base_change`): the kernel of the pulled-back quotient
81	is the pullback of the kernel — because `0 → I → O → O_D → 0` stays exact
82	after base change, `Tor_1` against the `T`-flat `O_D` vanishing (Kleiman §3,
83	functoriality note after `df:div`: "Since `D` is `T`-flat, `p_{X_T}^* I`
84	equals the ideal of `D_{T'}`") — and pullback preserves invertibility
85	(`IsLocallyTrivial.pullback`, Stacks 01HH).  The theorem carries a
86	quasi-coherence hypothesis on the source of the quotient (removable once
87	extension-closure of quasi-coherence, Stacks 01LA, is available; see the
88	declaration docstring), discharged here by `pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom` +
89	`Modules.unit_isQuasicoherent` since the source is the pulled-back unit.
90	The supporting lemmas — the Stacks 00HL algebra heart
91	`Module.Flat.rTensor_injective_of_exact`, the comparison map
92	`Modules.pullbackKernelComparison`, and the chart-shrinking lemmas — live in
93	`Picard/FlatKernelBase.lean`; the derivation of the pinned statement from
94	the isomorphism form of the comparison is
95	`Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial_of_isIso_kernelComparison` (§0).
96	
97	The functor laws are verbatim the pseudofunctor-coherence argument of
98	`Scheme.QuotFunctor` (`Modules.pullback_id_app_coherence`,
99	`Modules.pullback_comp_app_coherence_inv`), which was stated in
100	`QuotFunctorDef.lean` for arbitrary modules and so applies to the unit.

729	/-! ## §2. Families of relative effective divisors -/
730	
731	variable {S X : Scheme.{u}}
732	
733	/-- A **family of relative effective divisors on `X ×_S T / T`** (Kleiman §3
734	Def. `df:red`/`df:div`, in the quotient encoding — see the module docstring):
735	a `T`-flat, finitely presented quotient `q` of the structure sheaf of the
736	relative product `X_T = X ×_S T` with proper support, whose kernel ideal
737	`I = ker q` is invertible (`Scheme.LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial`).  The
738	associated divisor is the schematic support `D` of `F = O_{X_T}/I = O_D`;
739	conversely a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ X_T` yields the family
740	`q : O_{X_T} ↠ O_D`.
741	
742	The source of `q` is stated as the pullback of the unit module `O_X` along
743	the first projection — canonically isomorphic to `O_{X_T}` — verbatim the
744	`E`-slot of `Scheme.QuotFamily` at `E = O_X`, so the Quot-family base-change
745	lemmas and pseudofunctor-coherence functor laws apply unchanged.  The fields
746	`isFinitePresentation` and `properSupport` are automatic for divisors on a
747	`T`-proper `X_T` (the FGA regime); see the module docstring. -/
748	structure DivFamily (π : X ⟶ S) (T : Over S) : Type (u + 1) where
749	  /-- The structure sheaf `O_D` of the divisor, as a quotient module on the
750	  relative product `X ×_S T`. -/
751	  F : (Limits.pullback π T.hom).Modules
752	  /-- `F` is finitely presented (automatic for an invertible ideal's
753	  quotient; kept to match the Quot-family shape). -/
754	  isFinitePresentation : F.IsFinitePresentation
755	  /-- `F = O_D` is flat over `T` — the divisor is a *relative* effective
756	  divisor (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:red`). -/
757	  flat : CoherentSheafFlat (pullback.snd π T.hom) F
758	  /-- The schematic support (the divisor `D` itself) is proper over `T`
759	  (automatic when `π` is proper; kept to match the Quot-family shape). -/
760	  properSupport : Modules.HasProperSupport (pullback.snd π T.hom) F
761	  /-- The quotient map `O_{X_T} ⟶ O_D` (source stated as the pulled-back
762	  unit, as in `QuotFamily` with `E = O_X`). -/
763	  q : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj
764	      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) ⟶ F
765	  /-- The quotient map is an epimorphism. -/
766	  epi : Epi q
767	  /-- **The divisor condition** (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:red`): the kernel ideal
768	  `I = ker q` is invertible, i.e. locally trivial of rank one. -/
769	  kerLocallyTrivial : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (Limits.kernel q)

771	namespace DivFamily

773	variable {π : X ⟶ S}
774	
775	/-- Two families of divisors are **equivalent** when an isomorphism of the
776	target sheaves commutes with the quotient maps — equivalently, when
777	`ker q = ker q'` as subobjects of `O_{X_T}`, i.e. when they cut out the same
778	closed subscheme (same convention as `QuotFamily.Rel`). -/
779	def Rel {T : Over S} (x y : DivFamily π T) : Prop :=
780	  ∃ f : x.F ≅ y.F, x.q ≫ f.hom = y.q
781	
782	lemma rel_refl {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T) : x.Rel x :=
783	  ⟨Iso.refl _, Category.comp_id _⟩
784	
785	lemma rel_symm {T : Over S} {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y) : y.Rel x := by
786	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h
787	  exact ⟨f.symm, by rw [Iso.symm_hom, Iso.comp_inv_eq]; exact hf.symm⟩
788	
789	lemma rel_trans {T : Over S} {x y z : DivFamily π T}
790	    (h1 : x.Rel y) (h2 : y.Rel z) : x.Rel z := by
791	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h1; obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := h2
792	  exact ⟨f ≪≫ g,
793	    (congrArg (x.q ≫ ·) (Iso.trans_hom f g)).trans <|
794	      (Category.assoc x.q f.hom g.hom).symm.trans <|
795	        (congrArg (· ≫ g.hom) hf).trans hg⟩
796	
797	/-- The equivalence-of-families setoid. -/
798	instance setoid (π : X ⟶ S) (T : Over S) : Setoid (DivFamily π T) where
799	  r := Rel
800	  iseqv := ⟨rel_refl, rel_symm, rel_trans⟩
801	
802	/-- The **pullback action** on a family of divisors along `ψ : T' ⟶ T` of
803	`Over S`: pull the sheaf and the quotient map back along
804	`quotBaseMap π ψ : X_{T'} ⟶ X_T`, matching the `O`-side through
805	`pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)` — exactly
806	`QuotFamily.pullbackAlong` at `E = O_X`.  The divisor condition base-changes
807	by `Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial`
808	(`lem:relative_divisor_base_change`). -/
809	noncomputable def pullbackAlong {T T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T)
810	    (x : DivFamily π T) : DivFamily π T' where
811	  F := (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).obj x.F
812	  isFinitePresentation :=
813	    Modules.pullback_isFinitePresentation _ x.F x.isFinitePresentation
814	  flat := fun {_} hU {_} hV e =>
815	    CoherentSheafFlat.of_isPullback (quotBaseSquare π ψ) x.F
816	      (letI := x.isFinitePresentation; inferInstance) x.flat hU hV e
817	  properSupport :=
818	    Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback (quotBaseSquare π ψ) x.F
819	      x.isFinitePresentation x.properSupport
820	  q := (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
821	      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv ≫
822	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q
823	  epi :=
824	    @CategoryTheory.epi_comp _ _ _ _ _
825	      (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
826	        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv inferInstance
827	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q)
828	      (@CategoryTheory.Functor.map_epi _ _ _ _
829	        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)) inferInstance _ _ x.q x.epi)
830	  kerLocallyTrivial :=
831	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial.of_iso
832	      (kernelIsIsoComp
833	        (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
834	          (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv
835	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q)).symm
836	      (Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial (quotBaseSquare π ψ) x.q x.epi
837	        (pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (pullback.fst π T.hom)
838	          (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) inferInstance)
839	        x.isFinitePresentation x.flat x.kerLocallyTrivial)
840	
841	/-- The pullback action respects the equivalence relation. -/
842	lemma pullbackAlong_rel {T T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T)
843	    {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y) :
844	    (pullbackAlong ψ x).Rel (pullbackAlong ψ y) := by
845	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h
846	  refine ⟨(Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).mapIso f, ?_⟩
847	  change ((pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
848	        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv ≫
849	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q) ≫
850	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map f.hom
851	    = (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
852	        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv ≫
853	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map y.q
854	  rw [Category.assoc, ← (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map_comp]
855	  exact congrArg
856	    (fun m => (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
857	        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv ≫
858	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map m) hf

864	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
865	/-- The **relative-divisor functor** `Div_{X/S}` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`):
866	the contravariant functor `(Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1)` sending an `S`-scheme
867	`T → S` to the set of relative effective divisors on `X_T/T` — encoded as
868	equivalence classes of families of invertible-kernel quotients of `O_{X_T}`
869	(`Scheme.DivFamily`; two families are identified iff `ker q = ker q'`, i.e.
870	iff they cut out the same divisor) — and a morphism to the pullback of
871	families (`DivFamily.pullbackAlong`).  The identity and composition laws are
872	the pseudofunctor coherence laws of the module pullback, packaged as
873	`Scheme.Modules.pullback_id_app_coherence` and
874	`Scheme.Modules.pullback_comp_app_coherence_inv` in `QuotFunctorDef.lean`. -/
875	noncomputable def DivFunctor (π : X ⟶ S) :
876	    (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1) where
877	  obj T := Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T.unop)
878	  map {T T'} g := TypeCat.ofHom (Quotient.map (DivFamily.pullbackAlong g.unop)
879	    (fun _ _ h => DivFamily.pullbackAlong_rel g.unop h))
880	  map_id T := by
881	    ext z
882	    induction z using Quotient.ind with
883	    | _ x =>
884	      change Quotient.mk _ (DivFamily.pullbackAlong (𝟙 T.unop) x) = Quotient.mk _ x
885	      refine Quotient.sound ⟨(Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr (quotBaseMap_id π T.unop)).app x.F ≪≫
886	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackId _).app x.F, ?_⟩
887	      change ((pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π (𝟙 T.unop))
888	            (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv ≫
889	          (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π (𝟙 T.unop))).map x.q) ≫
890	          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr (quotBaseMap_id π T.unop)).hom.app x.F ≫
891	          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackId _).hom.app x.F
892	        = x.q
893	      rw [Category.assoc,
894	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr (quotBaseMap_id π T.unop)).hom.naturality_assoc x.q,
895	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackId _).hom.naturality x.q]
896	      have key := Scheme.Modules.pullback_id_app_coherence (quotBaseMap_id π T.unop)
897	        (quotBaseMap_fst π (𝟙 T.unop)) (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)
898	      simp only [pullbackTriangleIso, Iso.trans_inv, Iso.app_inv, Category.assoc]
899	      rw [reassoc_of% key]
900	      rfl

925	          x.q,
926	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (quotBaseMap π h.unop)
927	          (quotBaseMap π g.unop)).inv.naturality x.q]

8	/-!
9	# The divisor functor (DD-2 S6b)
10	
11	The one-screen functor packaging of the locally certified divisor vehicle
12	(`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §6, spelling (A) of I-0222, co-signed by the DD-R lane):
13	
14	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctor`: `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`, with object values
15	  `divFamZar C π n T` and action `divFamZar.map` — the `picEtFunctor` house pattern.
16	  Type-valued: degree-`n` divisor families carry no group structure.
17	
18	This is the functor `divRep` is stated against (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 8,
19	Addendum 1).  The sheaf halves are consumed as-is from
20	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarSheaf` (`ext_of_le_cover` /
21	`existsUnique_glue_of_le_cover`), the pic0/01JJ precedent.
22	-/

24	set_option autoImplicit false
25	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

27	depth must be set in-file for the faithful per-file check. -/

31

33	
34	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
35	
36	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
37	
38	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

41	/-- **The divisor functor** (DD-2 S6b, the pinned name): the locally certified
42	degree-`n` divisor families as a presheaf of types on the slice over `Spec k`,
43	with the glued restriction `divFamZar.map` along arbitrary test morphisms — the
44	`picDegLayerFunctor` house pattern. -/
45	noncomputable def divFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u where
46	  obj T := divFamZar C π n T.unop
47	  map g := ↾divFamZar.map C π n g.unop
48	  map_id T := by
49	    ext s U
50	    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZar C π n T.unop => z.1 U) (divFamZar.map_id C π n s)
51	  map_comp {T T' T''} g h := by
52	    ext s U
53	    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZar C π n T''.unop => z.1 U)
54	      (divFamZar.map_comp C π n g.unop h.unop s)
55

57	lemma divFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
58	    (divFunctor C π n).obj T = divFamZar C π n T.unop :=
59	  rfl

62	lemma divFunctor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
63	    (s : divFamZar C π n T.unop) :
64	    (divFunctor C π n).map g s = divFamZar.map C π n g.unop s :=
65	  rfl
66	
67	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# DDR-9.F7 — the affine-to-general lift, completed
10	
11	`Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean` builds the general-test pullback `pullGlobal` of an
12	affine divisor package `DivRepAffinePullback` together with its naturality in the
13	test object.  This file supplies the other half — the general-test classifier — and
14	assembles the `DivRepGlobalData` of `Picard/DivRepKit.lean`, hence the divisor
15	representability of `divFunctor C π g` by `DivScheme`.
16	
17	The classifier is obtained by gluing the landed affine classifiers `divRepClassifyZar`
18	over the affine opens of the test.  Two observations make the gluing cheap:
19	
20	* The affine opens of a scheme form a **locally directed** open cover
21	  (`Scheme.directedAffineCover`), so a morphism glues from compatibility with the
22	  transition maps alone (`Scheme.OpenCover.glueMorphismsOverOfLocallyDirected`); no
23	  condition on the — in general non-affine — overlaps is needed.
24	* The required compatibility is naturality of `divRepClassifyZar` in the test algebra.
25	  That naturality is not proved from the characterizing clause: it is *forced* by the
26	  affine package, since `D.pull` is injective (`DivRepAffinePullback.equiv`) and natural
27	  (`D.pull_naturality`), so the classifier — its inverse — is natural as well.
28	
29	The results:
30	
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.classifyGlobal` — the general-test classifier,
32	  restricting at every affine open `W ⊆ T.left` to the affine classifier of the value
33	  `F.1 W` (`fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal`).
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.toGlobalData` — the `DivRepGlobalData` of the
35	  affine package: `pullGlobal` and `classifyGlobal` are mutually inverse on every test.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy` — **the divisor
37	  representability theorem in its conditional form**: an affine divisor package
38	  represents `divFunctor C π g` by `DivScheme`.
39	-/

120	/-! ## Naturality of the affine classifier -/
121	
122	/-- **The affine backward classifier is natural in the test algebra.**  This is not
123	proved from the characterizing clause: it is forced by the affine package, whose forward
124	map `D.pull` is injective and natural, so its inverse is natural too — concretely, the
125	base change of a classifier classifies the base-changed class, by
126	`D.isDivRepClassify_pull` at the base-changed morphism. -/
127	private theorem overSpecMap_comp_divRepClassifyZar
128	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
129	    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
130	    (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (F : DivFamZar C A pi g) :
131	    Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 A F
132	      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 B (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi F) := by
133	  have hpull : D.pull B
134	      (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 A F)
135	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi F := by
136	    rw [D.pull_naturality phi (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 A F),
137	      D.pull_classify A F]
138	  refine divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 _ _ ?_
139	  rw [← hpull]
140	  exact D.isDivRepClassify_pull B _
141	
142	/-! ## The general-test classifier -/
143	
144	/-- The affine classifiers of the values of `F`, transported to the open subschemes of
145	the affine opens of `T.left` — the family glued by `classifyGlobal`. -/
146	private noncomputable def classifyPiece
147	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
148	    (U : T.left.affineOpens) : U.1.toScheme ⟶ (DivOver).left :=
149	  U.2.isoSpec.hom ≫
150	    (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 Γ(T.left, U.1) (F.1 U)).left
151	
152	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
153	-- The rewrite chain unifies through the section-ring algebra towers over both affine
154	-- opens at once, so it exceeds the default elaboration budget (as in
155	-- `divFamZar.exists_isGlueValue`).
156	/-- The gluing datum: the family `classifyPiece` is compatible with the transition maps
157	of the directed cover of `T.left` by its affine opens.  This is naturality of the affine
158	classifier along the section restriction, applied to the coherence of `F`. -/
159	private theorem homOfLE_classifyPiece
160	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
161	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
162	    {U V : T.left.affineOpens} (hle : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
163	    T.left.homOfLE hle ≫ classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F V
164	      = classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F U := by
165	  have hres : (Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T hle)).left ≫ V.2.fromSpec
166	      = U.2.fromSpec :=
167	    congrArg CategoryTheory.Over.Hom.left (Over.fromSpecAffine_resAlgHom (T := T) hle)
168	  have hkey : U.2.isoSpec.hom ≫ (Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T hle)).left
169	      = T.left.homOfLE hle ≫ V.2.isoSpec.hom := by
170	    rw [← cancel_mono V.2.fromSpec, Category.assoc, Category.assoc, hres,
171	      isoSpec_hom_fromSpec, isoSpec_hom_fromSpec, Scheme.homOfLE_ι]
172	  have hcl : (Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T hle)).left
173	        ≫ (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 Γ(T.left, V.1) (F.1 V)).left
174	      = (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 Γ(T.left, U.1) (F.1 U)).left := by
175	    rw [← CategoryTheory.Over.comp_left,
176	      overSpecMap_comp_divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D, F.compat U V hle]
177	  rw [classifyPiece, classifyPiece, ← Category.assoc, ← hkey, Category.assoc, hcl]
178	
179	/-- The gluing datum: each piece lies over `Spec k` compatibly with the test `T`. -/
180	private theorem classifyPiece_over
181	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
182	    (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
183	    classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F U ≫ (DivOver).hom = U.1.ι ≫ T.hom := by
184	  rw [classifyPiece, Category.assoc, CategoryTheory.Over.w,
185	    ← CategoryTheory.Over.w (Over.fromSpecAffine T U), ← Category.assoc]
186	  exact congrArg (· ≫ T.hom) (isoSpec_hom_fromSpec U.2)
187	
188	private theorem classifyPiece_trans
189	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
190	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
191	    {U V : T.left.directedAffineCover.I₀} (hij : U ⟶ V) :
192	    Scheme.Cover.trans T.left.directedAffineCover hij
193	        ≫ classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F V
194	      = classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F U := by
195	  rw [Subsingleton.elim hij (homOfLE (leOfHom hij)),
196	    Scheme.directedAffineCover_trans (leOfHom hij)]
197	  exact homOfLE_classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F (leOfHom hij)
198	
199	/-- **The general-test classifier of the affine package**: the affine classifiers of the
200	values of `F` at the affine opens of `T.left`, glued over the locally directed cover of
201	`T.left` by its affine opens.  The gluing datum is the compatibility with the transition
202	maps `T.left.homOfLE`, which is naturality of `divRepClassifyZar`
203	(`overSpecMap_comp_divRepClassifyZar`) applied to the coherence of `F`. -/
204	noncomputable def classifyGlobal
205	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
206	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) : T ⟶ DivOver :=
207	  Scheme.OpenCover.glueMorphismsOverOfLocallyDirected (X := T) (Y := DivOver)
208	    T.left.directedAffineCover (classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F)
209	    (fun {_U _V} hij => classifyPiece_trans hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F hij)
210	    (classifyPiece_over hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F)
211	
212	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
213	/-- The general-test classifier restricts on the open subscheme of an affine open to the
214	transported affine classifier there. -/
215	private theorem ι_classifyGlobal
216	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
217	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
218	    (W : T.left.affineOpens) :
219	    W.1.ι ≫ (classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
220	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F).left
221	      = classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F W :=
222	  Scheme.OpenCover.map_glueMorphismsOverOfLocallyDirected_left
223	    (X := T) (Y := DivOver) T.left.directedAffineCover
224	    (classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F)
225	    (fun {_U _V} hij => classifyPiece_trans hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F hij)
226	    (classifyPiece_over hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F) W
227	
228	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
229	/-- **The characterizing property of the general-test classifier**: its restriction to
230	the affine-open test object presented by `W` is the affine classifier of the value of `F`
231	at `W`. -/
232	theorem fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal
233	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
234	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
235	    (W : T.left.affineOpens) :
236	    Over.fromSpecAffine T W ≫ classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
237	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F
238	      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 Γ(T.left, W.1) (F.1 W) := by
239	  refine Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_
240	  change W.2.fromSpec ≫ _ = _
241	  rw [← IsAffineOpen.isoSpec_inv_ι, Category.assoc,
242	    ι_classifyGlobal hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F W, classifyPiece,
243	    Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
244	
245	/-! ## The two inverse laws -/
246	
247	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
248	/-- **The `pull_classify` law at an arbitrary test**: the general-test pullback of the
249	general-test classifier of `F` is `F`.  Both sides are sections of the Zariski vehicle,
250	so it suffices to compare at an affine open, where the characterizing property of the
251	classifier reduces the statement to the affine law `D.pull_classify`. -/
252	theorem pullGlobal_classifyGlobal
253	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
254	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) :
255	    pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
256	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D
257	        (classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1)
258	          (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F)
259	      = F := by
260	  refine divFamZar.ext fun W => ?_
261	  rw [pullGlobal_val, fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal, D.pull_classify]
262	
263	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
264	/-- **The `classify_pull` law at an arbitrary test**: the general-test classifier of the
265	general-test pullback of `v` is `v`.  Morphisms out of a test are separated by the
266	affine-open test objects, and at each of those the uniqueness theorem
267	`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`, applied to `D.isDivRepClassify_pull`,
268	identifies the affine classifier with the restriction of `v`. -/
269	theorem classifyGlobal_pullGlobal
270	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
271	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver) :
272	    classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
273	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D
274	        (pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
275	          (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v)
276	      = v := by
277	  refine hom_ext_fromSpecAffine _ _ fun W => ?_
278	  rw [fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal, pullGlobal_val]
279	  exact (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 _ _
280	    (D.isDivRepClassify_pull _ (Over.fromSpecAffine T W ≫ v))).symm
281	
282	/-! ## The affine-to-general lift -/
283	
284	/-- **The affine-to-general lift of DDR-9.F7**: an affine divisor package determines the
285	general-test data of `DivRepGlobalData` — the pullback is `pullGlobal`, the classifier is
286	`classifyGlobal`, the two inverse laws are `classifyGlobal_pullGlobal` and
287	`pullGlobal_classifyGlobal`, and naturality in the test object is `pullGlobal_comp`. -/
288	noncomputable def toGlobalData
289	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2) :
290	    DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 where
291	  pull {_T} v := pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1)
292	    (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v
293	  classify {_T} F := classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
294	    (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F
295	  classify_pull {_T} v := classifyGlobal_pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO)
296	    (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v
297	  pull_classify {_T} F := pullGlobal_classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO)
298	    (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F
299	  pull_comp {_T _T'} f v := pullGlobal_comp (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
300	    (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D f v
301	
302	/-- **Divisor representability from an affine package** (DDR-9.F7): an affine divisor
303	package represents the locally certified divisor functor `divFunctor C π g` by
304	`DivScheme`.  This is the composite of the affine-to-general lift with the categorical
305	packaging `DivRepGlobalData.representableBy`. -/
306	noncomputable def representableBy
307	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2) :
308	    (divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver :=
309	  DivRepGlobalData.representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1)
310	    (b2 := b2)
311	    (toGlobalData (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
312	      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D)
313	
314	end DivRepAffinePullback
315	
316	end Curve
317

must provide every field of `DivRepGlobalData`.

/-!
# The `k'`-level representability datum `PicRepDatum` (DAT-glue → DAT-G handoff, DG-0)

The **frozen intermediate handoff shape** of the DAT-glue node
(`informal/w4-datglue-worksheet.md` §1/§3.3/§3.4; DG-0 row of §4).  The 01JJ
`RepresentableBy` assembly is honest only at a *separably closed* base `K_s` (DAT-B
staging finding, I-0248): the raw 01JJ output is a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor` at
`K_s`, not at the challenge base `k`.  The `K_s → k'` finite-level transfer (DAT-G0, the
worksheet-first mountain owned by DAT-glue; mini-spec `informal/spec-datg0.md`) lands its
output in this structure — a representation at a **finite separable** `k'/k` — which is
exactly the interface the downstream DAT-G lane (finite Galois / Speiser descent `k' → k`)
consumes.

`PicRepDatum` is deliberately the `JacobianData` shape *minus* the quasi-compactness
certificate (re-derived at `k'` by the same image-of-`DivScheme` argument, or inherited
a posteriori by DAT-J at `k`; worksheet §3.4) and *plus* the `[Algebra k k']` datum that
records how the intermediate field sits over the challenge base.

## Binder deviation from the worksheet §3.3 skeleton (RECORDED, forced by elaboration)

The worksheet §3.3 froze `structure PicRepDatum (k' : Type u) … [Algebra k k'] …` with `k`
an *ambient* `variable {k}`.  That does not elaborate for *consumers*: unlike
`JacobianData C` (where `C : Over (Spec (.of k))` pins `k`), here the explicit data pin
only `k'` (`C' : Over (Spec (.of k'))`), and `k` occurs solely inside `[Algebra k k']`, so
`PicRepDatum k' C'` leaves `k` an undetermined metavariable (`Algebra ?m k'` typeclass
stuck).  DG-0 therefore makes **`k` explicit** — `PicRepDatum k k' C'` — the minimal change
that keeps every field, instance, and the mathematical content of the frozen shape while
making `k` recoverable.  The frozen *math* (fields `J`/`rep`/`lft`, the four curve
instances, `[Algebra k k']`) is unchanged.

## The `pic0TypeFunctor`-vs-`JacobianData.rep` defeq note (worksheet §1.1, RECORDED)

The `rep` field is typed against `(pic0TypeFunctor C').RepresentableBy J`.  Since
`pic0TypeFunctor C'` is the `noncomputable abbrev`
`(pic0Functor C' ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
(`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`), this type is **definitionally** the `rep`-field type of
`JacobianData` (`JacobianData.lean`, whose `rep` is
`((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J`).  So
when `k' = k`, a `PicRepDatum` (with quasi-compactness re-supplied) transports into a
`JacobianData` with **no massage** — recorded machine-checked by the `example` below.
This is also why DAT-glue's raw 01JJ output `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
(`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`) is *directly* a `rep`-shaped datum: no `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
adaptation, no ε⁺-shift at assembly time (the shift lives inside DAT-C's `chartValue`).

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum k k' C'` — the frozen `k'`-level datum: representing
  object `J`, the honest `RepresentableBy` datum `rep` (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and
  the locally-of-finite-type certificate `lft` (carried from `K_s` along DAT-G0, worksheet
  §2.3/§3.3 step 3).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property in
  consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C' T`, natural against `pic0Map` (owns the
  `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq once, exactly as `JacobianData.homEquiv` does).

290	(Stacks 00HL affine-locally) at the fibre square: `T`-flatness of `O_D` is
291	what forbids the ideal from degenerating on special fibres. -/

293	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :

344	        (Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t))).g) :=
